title: A neural net, assembled one part at a time
card: Scroll and the net builds itself, one machine per beat. At the end it runs — because 'what each part does' and 'how the weights move' are two different questions and want two different pages.
lede: One concrete network: 784 inputs, one hidden layer of 128, ten outputs, 101,770 parameters. The article half answers what each moving part does. The console at the end answers the other question — how a correction at the output reaches a weight at the input.
handle: A forward pass and a backward pass run over the same machines in opposite directions. That is the whole idea, and it is exactly what a static layer diagram cannot show — which is why this page ends on a console instead of a picture.
source: arithmetic for a 784→128→10 MLP: 784×128 + 128 + 128×10 + 10 = 101,770 parameters. Every number on this page is that network's.
